  • the pass rate, the share of the checks that passed. Informational findings neither pass nor fail, so they are not counted;
  • how many findings there are per severity, and per category with the category's own pass rate. Select a category to show only its findings;
  • two views, Findings and Controls. The address keeps the one you opened (/settings/security/audit?view=controls), so you can link to it;
  • the findings, grouped by severity or by category, which you can filter by severity, category and text. Each one says what was found and, when there is something to do, how to fix it;
  • when the audit last ran.

The audit reads the live configuration every time it runs. After changing a setting or an environment variable (and restarting the platform when the variable needs it), select Re-run to check the result.

The platform also runs the audit on its own once an hour. A Critical or Warning finding it has never reported notifies every active administrator in the notification bell: one notification per run, naming the new findings, which opens the audit on them. Each finding is reported once, for good: it is not reported again when it escalates, disappears and comes back, or when Redis restarts, since what was reported is kept in the database. A run with no active administrator records nothing, so the first administrator still hears about every finding. The only finding reported a second time is a dismissed one that reopens (see below). The notification names the findings only; what they list (accounts, agents) stays on this page.

docs.title: Dismissing a finding
docs.text:
Some findings describe a choice you made on purpose: a protection you leave off, a setting the deployment needs. Select Dismiss finding on a Critical, Warning or Info finding to accept it, with an optional reason (up to 1,000 characters). A dismissed finding:

  • leaves the counts, the posture, the pass rate and the category breakdown, and no longer raises its control in the Controls view;
  • is never notified;
  • is listed under Dismissed findings at the bottom of the Findings view, collapsed, with who dismissed it, when, and why. Restore counts it again; a restored finding that was never notified is notified once, like a new one. The platform keeps who last dismissed a restored finding, at which severity and why, along with who restored it and when.

A dismissal holds for the severity it was made at. When a later run reports the finding at a higher severity (an Info that became a Warning, a Warning that became a Critical), it reopens: it counts again at once, and the finding says it was reopened, from which severity, and shows the dismissal it replaced. The next hourly run records the reopening and notifies every administrator once (dismissing or restoring any finding in the meantime records it too). Dismiss it again if the new severity is acceptable too.

Dismissals are stored in the database, apply to every administrator, and are recorded in the audit log (dismiss and restore by the administrator who made them, reopen by the platform). Scripts use PUT /api/v1/security-audit/findings/{id}/dismissal with an optional reason and DELETE on the same address to restore; both return the report. In the report, a dismissed finding carries dismissed (who, when, why, and the severity it was dismissed at), a reopened one carries reopened, and dismissed_count says how many were left out of summary and score. A finding the audit does not report now cannot be dismissed, nor can a Passed one.

docs.title: Accounts nobody signs in to
docs.text:
Deactivating an account in Admin > Users pauses the assignments and flows it owns, except company-managed ones, and reactivating it resumes them unchanged. Removing someone from the identity provider only stops their sign-in: their account stays active, and so do their automations, with their identity and their integrations. authentication.dormant_account_automations is a Warning that lists the active accounts that own an enabled assignment (on an enabled agent) or an active flow that is not company-managed, when nobody has signed in to them for 30 days, or ever for an account created more than 30 days ago: each with its last sign-in and what it owns. Deactivate the account of anyone who left, or transfer the agent (its assignments follow) or the flow to an active owner, or make it company-managed. While every such owner signed in within 30 days, the audit reports authentication.automation_owners_signed_in instead.

A sign-in is one the audit log records: a password (with its second factor when there is one), OIDC or SAML, an MCP OAuth authorization, or an XTM One Desktop sign-in confirmed in the browser (declining one is not a sign-in). A session lasts JWT_EXPIRE_MINUTES (7 days by default) and is not extended, so anyone using the web app signs in within the 30 days. API keys and the chat embedded in OpenCTI or OpenAEV do not sign in: an account used only through them is listed too.

docs.title: Nova semantic thresholds
docs.text: The semantics: thresholds of the Nova community rules were written for all-MiniLM-L6-v2. The platform scores them with its own embedding model and maps each score onto that model's scale when the model has a measured calibration (see Semantic-threshold calibration). While the Nova integration runs its full engine and an enabled platform rule has a semantics: pattern, the audit reports agents.nova_semantics_calibrated (Passed) on a calibrated model. On a model with no calibration it reports agents.nova_semantics_uncalibrated_block_rules, a Warning listing the Block rules among them, or agents.nova_semantics_uncalibrated, an Info, when they all only log. Switch those rules to Log on the Nova rules tab, or pick a calibrated embedding model for the semantics tier there. When the semantic model picked there is not used (chosen for another embedding provider, or returning no embedding), it also reports agents.nova_semantic_override_ignored, a Warning, and the findings above describe the platform embedding model the tier scores on instead.

docs.title: Reads with no account
docs.text:
An agent that browses the platform (the agent builder's read tools, template search) for a caller with no account - an anonymous channel sender, the public chat widget - sees only company-managed resources without Restrict access; what the agent itself is configured with stays its reach (see Channels). Three kinds of work with no account keep every company-managed resource, restricted ones included, and three Info findings list them while a company-managed resource has Restrict access on:

  • access.ownerless_assignments_restricted_reach: company-managed assignments that run with no user (an automatic trigger and no "run as" user) - set a "run as" user in each resource's audience;
  • access.global_mcp_key_restricted_reach: the agents the global MCP endpoint's platform key runs - expose there only agents meant for every key holder;
  • access.ownerless_evaluations_restricted_reach: evaluations with no owning user - give the evaluation an owner in each resource's audience.

docs.title: Personal credentials used by others
docs.text: An integration connected with a person's own credential - a connected account, a personal access token, an API key - lends it to everyone who can act with it: the people and groups the integration is shared with (a connected account only once its holder shared it), and the audience of every agent, assignment, flow, knowledge base, skill or General Assistant list holding it, whose runs use it as bound. access.personal_credentials_lent is an Info finding listing each such integration, whose credential it is, through what it is lent and how many people (or a public widget link, people with no account on a channel, the holders of the platform MCP key) act with it; it also lists an integration whose owner acts with an account the previous owner connected. A company-managed integration's credential is the company's and is not listed. Review each in the integration's Sharing and access section, and where others should not act as its holder, turn on Don't share my connected account, switch the agent to per-user integrations, or give the work a company-managed integration.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
A security control is one switch that makes the platform safer when set: an environment variable, or a setting stored in Settings. The Controls view lists every control that applies to this platform (the SSO controls, for example, only once SSO is on) with its state:

  • Enforced - set to the value that protects.
  • Monitoring - it records what it would block without blocking it. The tool-call budget is one: without the strict cut, a batch that crosses the budget still runs, and the overshoot is logged and recorded on the run's trace. The content security policy is another in its default report-only mode: browsers block nothing and report what it would block (see Security headers).
  • Off - neither.

Each control shows its setting, its current value next to the value that enforces it, Opt-in when the platform default leaves it off, and the most severe finding about it. A control that is off while a warning or a critical finding is about it comes first, then the other controls that are off, then those that monitor and those that are enforced. Open a control to read what enforcing it changes for users, where what it would block is recorded (read it before enforcing), how to change it, the platform default and the findings about it. Filter the controls by state, category and text.

A control set by an environment variable is changed by setting the variable and restarting the platform; a stored control is changed on the Settings page it names, and a per-agent control (visitor uploads on the public chat widgets) on each agent it counts. A control that is also one of the security options can be changed there too, with no restart: its details say where its value comes from (its environment variable, a value saved in Security options, or the default) and link to the field (Configure <option>), unless its variable is set - the control then shows the Env badge, since the variable wins. A control XTM One fixes, the quota fail mode, is always enforced in xtm_one mode: its details say it cannot be changed.

Control Setting Enforced when What enforcing it changes authentication.invitation_expiry INVITATION_EXPIRE_HOURS <= 168 An invitation link lasts a week at most unless the administrator who creates it picks another lifetime: an invitee who waits longer needs a new one. authentication.local_sign_in local_auth_enabled in Settings > Security > Authentication (Local Authentication) false Every sign-in goes through SSO, administrators included: password sign-in and self-registration are refused (an invitation still registers its invitee). Keep an administrator who signs in through SSO before turning it off, since an identity provider outage then locks everyone out. authentication.min_password_length MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH >= 12 A password set from then on (registration, invitation, password change, a local account an administrator creates) needs at least that many characters, with a letter and a digit as today. Existing passwords keep working until they change. authentication.password_reset_expiry PASSWORD_RESET_EXPIRE_HOURS 1 A password reset link stops working an hour after it is sent: someone who opens the email later asks for a new one. authentication.platform_token_audiences XTM_AUTH_ACCEPTED_AUDIENCES empty A token a registered OpenCTI, OpenAEV or OpenCRQ signs a user in with is accepted only when it is addressed to BASE_URL, XTM One's identity (published at /xtm/auth/metadata): a platform version that addresses its tokens to the internal URL it reaches XTM One on is refused until it reads that document. authentication.self_registration registration_enabled in Settings > Security > Authentication (Allow local registration) false Nobody can create an account from the sign-in page: accounts come from an administrator, an invitation or SSO. authentication.session_lifetime JWT_EXPIRE_MINUTES <= 1440 People sign in again every day, and a stolen session token stops working within a day. JWT_EXPIRE_MINUTES is marked internal in the configuration and is not documented for operators: it is read like any variable, but it is not a supported setting. authentication.sso_account_creation oidc_auto_create_users, saml_auto_create_users, allowed_domains in Settings > Security > Authentication (On-the-fly user creation, Allowed email domains) false, or allowed email domains set SSO no longer creates an account for everyone the identity provider authenticates. With On-the-fly user creation off, only people who already have an account, matched by SSO subject or email, can sign in through SSO; anyone else is refused until an administrator or an invitation creates the account. With allowed email domains set, SSO creates an account only for an email address, as the identity provider asserts it, at one of those domains. Existing accounts keep signing in whatever their domain. With XTM_HUB_ADMIN_GROUP set, the XTM Hub decides who may sign in through OIDC. authentication.sso_auto_admin oidc_auto_admin_new_users, saml_auto_admin_new_users in Settings > Security > Authentication (Automatically admin users) false People who sign in through SSO keep the role an administrator gave them. While it is on, everyone who signs in through that method is made an administrator, existing accounts included and at every sign-in; turning it off demotes nobody. With XTM_HUB_ADMIN_GROUP set, the XTM Hub decides the role of an OIDC sign-in instead. agents.tool_result_guard_scope PROMPT_GUARD_SCANNED_TOOLS the tools that return outside content While a prompt guard (Nova) is connected, it evaluates what the listed tools return to an agent, the text of the files they attach included, and records each rule match in the audit log. The evaluation runs beside the agent, so it adds no wait unless tool results a block rule matches are also withheld. agents.tool_result_guard_blocking PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_TOOL_RESULTS true A screened tool result that a block rule matches is withheld: the agent reads a short refusal naming the tool instead, without the files the result carried. The agent then waits for the guard's verdict on each screened result before it continues. Monitoring while tools are screened and it is off: each match is recorded, the result reaches the agent. access.agent_tools_strict_admin_access AGENT_TOOLS_STRICT_ADMIN_ACCESS true An admin's agent tools (the agent builder in chat and on the XTM One MCP server, the work-items delegation) read, trigger, edit, delete or add assignments only where the admin's own, group-shared and company-managed objects reach; admins keep full access through the UI and the REST API. agents.prompt_guard_blocks_general_assistant PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_GENERAL_ASSISTANT true While a prompt guard (Nova) is connected, a General Assistant message one of its block rules matches is refused with the guard's message before the model is called, instead of being answered. A false positive refuses a colleague's question. agents.prompt_guard_blocks_public_widget PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_PUBLIC_WIDGET true While a prompt guard (Nova) is connected, a public chat widget message one of its block rules matches is refused with the guard's message before the model is called, instead of being answered. A false positive refuses a visitor, who has nobody to ask. agents.prompt_guard_model_output PROMPT_GUARD_MODEL_OUTPUT block While a prompt guard (Nova) is connected, every model answer is evaluated before it is delivered, and one of its block rules matches is replaced by a withheld notice: answers take the evaluation's time longer. A streamed answer (web chat, the streaming chat embedded in OpenCTI / OpenAEV, the widget's stream) has already been shown, so it is only audited. log is the monitoring state. network.trust_proxy_headers TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS false X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto count only from a proxy FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS names, never from any peer. Declare the proxy there first: without it, rate limits bucket every caller under the proxy's address and HTTPS behind it is unconfirmed. network.client_ip_strict CLIENT_IP_STRICT true Every client address is keyed, logged and stored in canonical form - port, brackets and IPv6 zone index dropped, an IPv4-mapped address read as IPv4, IPv6 lowercase - so one client is one rate-limit key whatever the proxy wrote. A client whose address arrived in another spelling has its current rate-limit window restart once. network.rate_limit_ipv6_prefix RATE_LIMIT_IPV6_PREFIX <= 64 The per-IP rate limits key a native IPv6 client on its network (its /64 at 64) instead of its address, so rotating addresses within it draws no fresh bucket. Every device of one /64, a corporate IPv6 LAN included, then shares one budget. network.credential_transport_strict CREDENTIAL_TRANSPORT_STRICT true Runner enrollment (POST /runners/enroll), MCP OAuth client registration (POST /mcp/oauth/register) and the MCP OAuth token endpoint (POST /mcp/oauth/token) refuse a request the platform cannot confirm arrived over HTTPS - 403 https required, the OAuth invalid_client_metadata error and the OAuth invalid_request error - instead of serving it. Behind a TLS-terminating proxy, FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS must name it first, or every runner enrollment, MCP client registration and MCP token request through it is refused; a deployment served over plain HTTP can no longer enroll runners, register MCP clients or issue MCP tokens. web.content_security_policy CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY_MODE enforce Browsers refuse to run a script or load a resource the platform's pages do not need, a script injected past the output checks or added by a proxy or CDN included, and to show the pages in the iframe of a site the policy does not allow. The API reference, the Teams tab and the Office add-in stay report-only. web.cors_origins CORS_ORIGINS a list without * Only the listed origins may call the API from a browser page; a page on any other origin is refused by the browser. web.csp_frame_ancestors CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY_FRAME_ANCESTORS a list without *, a bare scheme or a wildcard host Once CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY_MODE=enforce, only the platform itself, the sites listed and, behind a registration token of the operator's own, the registered platforms may show its pages in an iframe: list a portal that embeds the platform before enforcing, or it is refused. web.public_widget_strict_rendering PUBLIC_WIDGET_STRICT_RENDERING true Public chat widget answers show only the images the platform serves (any other image becomes a link), open every link in a new tab, and drop inline styles, SVG, MathML and links other than http(s), mailto and tel. web.public_widget_uploads web_uploads_enabled on each agent, in Agents > the agent > Configuration > Web Exposure (Allow visitor uploads) false on every widget Visitors of the public chat widgets, who have no account, can only type: a widget that let them attach a document or an image to a message no longer offers it. The files already attached stay readable by the agent until the retention deletes them. Its value is how many live widgets allow uploads; see Visitor uploads on the public chat widget. integrations.oauth_token_url_strict OAUTH_TOKEN_URL_STRICT true Every OAuth token request (code exchange and refresh, for integrations and MCP servers) and every save of a token URL also refuses a token URL whose host is, or resolves to, a loopback, link-local, unspecified, reserved or multicast address, and any scheme but http(s); private networks stay allowed. An integration or MCP server whose token URL is on loopback stops exchanging and refreshing tokens until the URL points at another address of its identity provider or, on a development machine, its origin is listed in the loopback token URL origins. integrations.oauth_token_dev_trusted_origins OAUTH_TOKEN_DEV_TRUSTED_ORIGINS empty Under the strict OAuth token URL checks, every OAuth token request (code exchange and refresh, for integrations and MCP servers) refuses a token URL that resolves to a loopback address; only local development against an identity provider on the same machine needs the list. Without the strict checks the list has no effect. agents.nova_llm_every_condition NOVA_LLM_MAX_CONDITIONS 0 While the Nova integration runs its full engine, every distinct llm: condition of the enabled rules is put to the model on each message it screens, one call per condition, as it always was. With a ceiling set, the conditions past it are not asked (those of block rules are kept first), and a rule resting on one cannot fire through that tier. assignments.webhook_require_secret WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_SECRET true A delivery to an assignment webhook with no secret configured is refused (401) instead of run: such an assignment stops triggering until it has a secret and the sender signs with it. tools.code_interpreter_disabled DISABLE_CODE_INTERPRETER true Agents and the General Assistant can no longer run Python in the code interpreter. tools.code_interpreter_extra_modules CODE_INTERPRETER_EXTRA_ALLOWED_MODULES empty The code interpreter keeps its whole module blocklist: code it runs cannot open network connections (it shares the host's network). tools.custom_tool_extra_modules CUSTOM_TOOL_EXTRA_ALLOWED_MODULES empty Python custom tools keep their whole module blocklist: in the subprocess fallback they cannot open network connections. tools.custom_tool_node_permission CUSTOM_TOOL_NODE_PERMISSION true A JavaScript custom tool run in the subprocess fallback gets no file system, child process, worker thread or native addon access (Node.js 24 or later); the network stays available. tools.custom_tool_sandbox CUSTOM_TOOL_SANDBOX docker or opensandbox Custom tools run in the hardened Docker container or an OpenSandbox container only: when that is unreachable they fail instead of falling back to a plain subprocess. tools.custom_tools_disabled DISABLE_CUSTOM_TOOLS true No custom tool (JavaScript or Python written by a user) runs anywhere: chat, assignments, flows and tests. tools.custom_variables_disabled DISABLE_CUSTOM_VARIABLES true The Variables feature is refused: its API and the agent builder's variable tools. tools.runner_result_bound RUNNER_MAX_RESULT_BYTES > 0 A runner file read never asks for more than the bound or 256 KiB, whichever is larger (text up to 256 KiB comes back inline, which the bound does not cap), and a larger file result is refused, so an agent cannot make a runner read a large file into memory. tools.runner_strict_path_confinement RUNNER_STRICT_PATH_CONFINEMENT true A restricted runner refuses a file command whose path leads outside its allowed folders through a symbolic link, junction or mount point, instead of running it with a warning (runners from this release or later). tools.svg_strict_rendering SVG_STRICT_RENDERING true An SVG a model is shown that declares an XML entity or references anything outside itself (a file path, a URL, another document) is not rendered at all, instead of being rendered with that reference dropped. Nothing is fetched or read from disk in either mode. tools.tool_call_budget_strict AGENT_LOOP_MAX_TOOL_CALLS_STRICT true A parallel batch of tool calls that crosses a run's budget runs only the calls that still fit; the others are answered "Not executed" instead of running. mcp.a2a_dev_trusted_origins A2A_CLIENT_DEV_TRUSTED_ORIGINS empty The A2A client reaches every partner over HTTPS at an address its destination guard accepts; only two deployments tested on one machine need the list. mcp.a2a_insecure_loopback A2A_ALLOW_INSECURE_LOOPBACK false A plain HTTP request from 127.0.0.1 or ::1 no longer counts as encrypted on the A2A surface. Behind a reverse proxy on the same host every partner request arrives from loopback, so the setting would waive HTTPS for all of them. mcp.dynamic_client_registration MCP_DCR_ENABLED false MCP clients can no longer register themselves (POST /mcp/oauth/register answers 403): an MCP client such as Claude Desktop or Cursor then needs an API key. Clients registered before keep working. mcp.outbound_dynamic_client_registration MCP_OUTBOUND_DCR_ENABLED false The platform no longer registers itself with a remote MCP server's authorization server: connecting an OAuth MCP server needs a client ID provisioned by hand. mcp.test_only_insecure_transport_peers TEST_ONLY_INSECURE_TRANSPORT_PEERS empty No network is exempted from the A2A HTTPS requirement: the list exists for the end-to-end test suite only. mcp.xtm_mcp_server xtm_mcp_enabled in Settings > MCP Endpoint false External MCP clients no longer reach this instance's own tools at /mcp/xtm: traces, the agent builder, knowledge search and skills, each within the caller's own rights. llm.trace_payloads trace_store_payloads, trace_storage_enabled in Settings > Observability (Store full payloads, Enable local trace storage) false, or trace storage off LLM traces no longer keep what was said: each call's prompts, answers, tool arguments and tool results are dropped, and an error message keeps its first 200 characters. Traces still show the timings, token counts, cost, model, tool names and status; with trace storage off, no trace is stored at all. It applies to the traces written from then on, on every server within seconds: traces stored before keep what they hold until the retention deletes them, and the Langfuse export, while it is on, still receives each call's payloads. infrastructure.debug_mode DEBUG false SQL statements are no longer echoed to the log with the tokens and encrypted values they carry, loopback no longer counts as HTTPS, password reset links are no longer written to the log when no SMTP server is set, and development-only tools are gone. infrastructure.quota_fail_mode QUOTA_FAIL_MODE closed While the quota store cannot be reached, agentic executions are refused instead of running unmetered; a due assignment run or background task is held until the store answers again. Always enforced in xtm_one mode, where quotas are part of the licence and it cannot be changed; configurable in copilot / dev mode. infrastructure.rate_limit_fail_mode RATE_LIMIT_FAIL_MODE closed While Redis cannot be reached, rate-limited requests (sign-in, password reset, webhooks, chat messages) are refused with a 503 instead of passing unthrottled.

The Enable local trace storage and Store full payloads switches of Observability are one control, llm.trace_payloads: it is enforced while either is off. By default traces keep their payloads, which the audit reports as information with the retention period; with payloads or storage off, it reports the pass.

The same report is available to scripts at GET /api/v1/security-audit, for administrators only. Every finding carries an id (for example infrastructure.debug_mode) that stays the same from one run to the next, so a script can follow a finding without relying on its title, which may include a count, and a finding about a control names it in control. controls lists every control that applies with its state, its value, default and hardened value and whether it is an opt_in, and controls_summary counts the controls per state.

docs.title: Security options
docs.text:
Security options holds the platform-wide security switches: trusted proxy headers (prefer FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS), canonical client addresses, HTTPS required for runner enrollment and MCP tokens (off by default: served and logged as before) and the IPv6 rate-limit prefix length, what rate limits and quotas do when their store cannot be read, the password length and the reset / invitation link lifetimes, MCP client registration, the strict OAuth token URL checks and the loopback token URL origins used in development under them, the A2A partner origins trusted in development and the loopback exemption used in tests, required webhook secrets, required verification of integration notifications (Slack, Microsoft Graph and LinkedIn deliveries the platform cannot verify - the Microsoft Graph notifications of the Teams bot's private and shared channels included, see Microsoft Teams - and the admin OAuth app's deliveries to other integrations: accepted as before and reported while it is off, refused when it is on), strict widget rendering, strict runner folder confinement, strict admin access for agent tools, the prompt guard switches (whether it refuses the General Assistant and widget messages its block rules match, whether it evaluates model answers, the tools whose results it screens and whether it withholds what a block rule matches), the code interpreter / custom tools / custom variables switches and the sandbox module and Node.js settings. Select Configure, change what you need and Save; the reset button next to a saved value returns it to its default. Every change is recorded in the audit log and applies on every server within a few seconds.

Tools screened by the prompt guard is empty by default: no tool result is screened. While a company-managed Nova integration is connected, the guard evaluates what a listed tool returns to an agent, the text of the files the result attaches included (images excluded), and records each rule match in the audit log as a Security alert (surface tool_result). The result reaches the agent as it is, and the evaluation runs beside the agent, which does not wait for it. With Withhold tool results a guard rule blocks on, a screened result that a block rule matches is withheld instead - the agent reads a short refusal naming the tool, without the result's files - and the agent waits for the guard's verdict on each screened result before it continues. In Configure, pick the tools from the list: built-in tools by name, integration and MCP tools by the name the platform gives them, custom tools by their id, shown under their current name - a custom tool stays screened when its owner renames it, with nothing to update here. A listed entry that no tool carries anymore (a deleted custom tool, a server that no longer offers the tool) is flagged so it can be removed.

Each option can also be set by an environment variable, and the variable wins: an option set that way shows an Env badge and "Set by environment variable X", and cannot be changed here until the variable is removed from the deployment. The full list, with the variables and defaults, is in Configuration.

In XTM One, Quotas when their store is unreachable is always closed: quotas are part of the licence, so agentic work is refused while their store cannot be reached. A due automation is held instead - shown as Held, charged once it runs, and run by itself once the store answers again (bounded by AI_UNAVAILABLE_HOLD_MAX_SECONDS). A store that refuses the platform's credentials (a wrong password, an ACL denial) is a configuration error, not an outage: that work is refused at once. The option shows a Read-only badge with that reason and cannot be changed, and its variable, QUOTA_FAIL_MODE, has no effect (set to open, the platform ignores it and logs a warning at startup).

The options are grouped under the categories of the security audit (Authentication, Sharing and access, Network, Browser security, Integrations, Agents, Assignments, Tools, MCP and A2A, Infrastructure): each under the category of the control it is.

Every option is also a security control, reported in the audit's Controls view with the value it resolves to (variable, saved value, then default), where that value comes from, and the Env or Read-only badge of a locked one. An option the security audit checks links to its finding: Security audit next to it opens the audit on that finding. The other way round, a finding whose recommendation names one of these options names the field and links to it: Configure <option> opens Security options on that field, ready to change. A finding whose option is set by its variable names only the variable and has no link, since the variable is what to change.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication controls sign-in and identity behavior:

  • local authentication rules
  • registration policy
  • OpenID Connect
  • SAML 2.0
  • SAML group mapping
  • allowed email domains

See Authentication for every setting.

docs.title: Memory purge
docs.text: Memory purge permanently deletes every agent memory on the platform, for example after discovering a flaw in the memory system. The purge cannot be undone and is recorded in the audit log.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
Observability covers tracing and diagnostics.

In the current UI, this mainly includes:

  • Enable local trace storage: whether LLM traces are stored at all
  • Store full payloads: whether a trace keeps what was said (prompts, answers, tool arguments and tool results) or only its timings, token counts, cost, model, tool names and status
  • Trace retention (days): how long stored traces are kept
  • Langfuse configuration, the optional export to Langfuse, which the two switches above do not govern

A change to the two switches applies within a few seconds on every server, to the traces written from then on; traces already stored keep what they hold until the retention deletes them. See What a trace keeps.

Some deployments can expose more observability options than others.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
Quality defines the feedback criteria: what people score when they rate an agent's work, on top of the thumbs up or down. Once a criterion exists, the rating dialog asks for it after either thumb, and each score can be skipped.

A criterion has a kind, fixed once it is created:

  • Scale: a whole step between two bounds, such as 1 to 5
  • Categorical: one of a few options, each worth a score from 0 to 1 (a warm tone can be worth 1 and a cold one 0)
  • Numeric: any number between a minimum and a maximum

Each criterion also has a weight. A rating's weighted score is the weighted mean of its scores, each read on a common 0 to 1 scale; a rating with no score is worth its thumb (1 for up, 0 for down), and so is every rating while no criterion exists. A weight of 0 keeps a criterion visible without counting it, but the enabled criteria cannot all weigh 0.

Switch a criterion off to stop asking for it while keeping the scores already given. Deleting it also deletes every score given on it. The agent's Feedback tab shows, per criterion, how many scores it received, their average, their distribution, and the daily average over the last 30 days.

docs.title: What regular users should know
docs.text:
If you are not an administrator, you may only see AI Models and Channels & Bots, or even fewer options depending on deployment.

That does not mean your account is broken. It only means shared configuration is intentionally restricted.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: The AI Catalog page explains where you can browse published resources and add them to your account.

docs.title: Channels and bots
docs.text:
A channel is a messaging platform your users already work in. When a channel bot is connected, people can talk to an XTM One agent from Slack, Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, or Google Chat instead of opening the web interface, and agents can post messages back into those conversations.

Everything on this page is configured in Settings > Channels & Bots. The per-platform guides then walk through the external setup, one platform at a time.

docs.title: Supported channels
docs.text:
Channel Direction What you connect Web chat Built in Nothing — always available for every user and agent Slack Receive and publish A Slack app with a bot token and signing secret Microsoft Teams Receive and publish An Entra ID app registration, an Azure Bot resource, and a Teams app package WhatsApp Receive and publish A Meta app using the WhatsApp Business Cloud API Telegram Receive and publish A bot created with @BotFather Discord Receive and publish A Discord application with a bot token Google Chat Receive and publish A Google Chat app and a service account key

Web chat is listed in the same screen as Web Chat, with an Always Active badge. It needs no setup and cannot be disabled.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You need to be an administrator. Only admins can create, edit, or delete channel bots.
  • The deployment needs an active Agentic AI license. Without it, saving a channel bot is rejected.
  • The platform must be reachable from the internet over HTTPS. Every platform except Discord delivers messages to a webhook URL built from BASE_URL — see Configuration. A local or private address works for testing only if the messaging platform can reach it.
  • You need administrator rights on the messaging platform itself, or someone who has them. Most steps happen in the external console, not in XTM One.

docs.title: How a channel goes live
docs.text:
The same four steps apply to every platform.

  1. Create the app on the messaging platform. Each platform has its own console — the Slack app directory, the Azure portal, Meta for Developers, and so on. This is where you obtain the credentials and grant permissions.
  2. Connect the bot in XTM One. In Settings > Channels & Bots, select the platform and click Configure, then paste the credentials. Every value is encrypted before it is stored. The card switches to Connected once credentials are saved.
  3. Point the platform at the webhook URL. The connected card shows a Webhook URL you can copy under Receive. Paste it into the messaging platform's webhook or messaging endpoint setting. Discord is the exception — it opens its own outgoing connection and needs no webhook.
  4. Enable the channel on an agent. A newly connected bot does not answer anything yet. Open the agent, go to Configuration > Channels & Bots, enable the channel, and turn on Receive, Publish, or both.

Use the built-in setup guide

Each card in Settings > Channels & Bots has a Setup Guide button. It shows the same steps as the pages here, with the permission list and your deployment's real webhook URL already filled in — including a copy-ready Teams manifest.

docs.title: Receive and publish
docs.text:
Every connected bot has two independent capabilities, shown side by side on the bot card and again on each agent.

  • Receive covers incoming messages: someone writes in a channel or sends a direct message, and an agent answers.
  • Publish covers outgoing messages: an agent uses the bot's tools to post a message, reply in a thread, add a reaction, or upload a file on its own initiative — for example at the end of an assignment.

The two are separate on purpose. An agent can post daily summaries to a channel without ever listening to it, and it can answer questions in a channel without being allowed to post anywhere else.

The Publish capability comes from the bot tools listed on the card. Click the tool count to browse them and test one against the live connection before an agent uses it.

docs.title: Restricting which channels a bot can use
docs.text:
A bot has ambient authority: on the messaging platform it can reach every channel it has been invited to. Channel whitelists narrow that down inside XTM One.

Both lists are edited on the bot card and apply to every agent using the bot:

  • The Receive whitelist limits which channels the platform accepts incoming messages from. Messages from anywhere else are ignored silently.
  • The Publish whitelist limits which channels agents can send to. A blocked send fails with an explicit access-denied error rather than posting to the wrong place.

When a list is empty, no restriction applies at bot level — but a bot with no whitelist at all is reserved for company-managed agents. Non-admin users only see the bot on their own agents once at least one whitelist entry exists, so they cannot silently give a personal agent workspace-wide reach.

Each agent can then narrow the bot's scope further in its own Channels & Bots section. The effective scope is the overlap between the agent's selection and the bot whitelist, never more than the bot allows. Admins can grant an exception per agent with Bypass whitelist.

docs.title: Direct messages, mentions, and anonymous users
docs.text:
Three toggles decide when a bot answers at all. Each exists on the bot card and again on every agent, and the bot setting always wins.

Toggle What it does Precedence Allow private conversations Direct messages reach the agent even when receive channels are restricted If the bot has it off, no agent can turn it back on Only when mentioned In group channels, the bot answers only when it is explicitly @mentioned (not supported on WhatsApp) If the bot has it on, no agent can turn it off Allow anonymous users People without an XTM One account can talk to the agent If the bot has it off, no agent can turn it back on

A few consequences are worth knowing:

  • Direct messages always bypass Only when mentioned. Someone messaging the bot privately never has to mention it.
  • With Only when mentioned on, once the bot has answered in a thread it keeps following that thread for about 24 hours without needing a new mention. This works where the platform reports both mentions and threads — Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Google Chat. On Telegram and Discord the mention is detected but there is no thread tracking, so each new question needs its own mention.
  • Only when mentioned cannot be used on WhatsApp at all: the Cloud API does not report structured mentions, so the condition is never satisfied and the bot stays silent in groups. Leave it off there and scope the bot with the receive whitelist instead.
  • With Allow anonymous users on, the conversation is not attached to a user account. The agent still receives the sender's display name and platform identity as context. The General Assistant is never available anonymously — anonymous traffic is served by agents only.
  • An anonymous conversation reaches what the agent is configured with: its knowledge bases, integrations, handover targets and work-item peers, whatever their Restrict access setting. What it browses across the platform - the agent builder's read tools, template search - is limited to what every user sees: company-managed resources without Restrict access.
  • Anonymous messages count against the platform-wide agentic limits of your license (no per-user limit applies to them). When the platform is at its limit, the sender is told This service is at capacity right now. Please try again later. wherever the bot would otherwise have answered - where it stays silent, it stays silent. See Requests with no account.

Anonymous access is a public door

Turning on Allow anonymous users lets anyone who can reach the channel use the agent, its tools, and its knowledge bases. Restrict the agent's tools and knowledge accordingly, and prefer a dedicated agent for public channels.

docs.title: Commands inside a conversation
docs.text:
Users have two commands on external channels, and they are worth mentioning when you announce a new bot:

  • /reset or /new archives the current conversation and starts a fresh one, which is the way to clear context that has drifted.
  • /stop mutes the bot in the current thread for seven days. Mentioning the bot again lifts the mute immediately. It works where threads are tracked — Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, and WhatsApp groups. On WhatsApp the mute cannot be lifted early, since mentions are not detected there, so it lasts the full seven days.

docs.title: Files in replies
docs.text:
When an agent's answer on a channel includes a file — a report, an export, a generated image — the message carries a link to it. The link works without an XTM One sign-in for 24 hours, so treat it like the file itself.

  • PDFs, plain-text, Markdown and CSV files, WebVTT subtitles, JSON files (JSON Lines and +json types such as JSON-LD included), audio, video, and images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, TIFF, ICO, HEIC / HEIF, JPEG XL, JPEG 2000) open in the browser. A browser that cannot display or play a format, such as TIFF or HEIC outside Safari, or CSV and JSON Lines in Chrome, saves it instead.
  • HTML pages, SVG drawings, XML files, and every other type are downloaded, never opened: a file an agent or a user wrote can never run as a page on your platform's address.

docs.title: How the bot knows who is talking
docs.text:
XTM One matches the sender to an account by email address:

  • Slack and Google Chat provide the email directly, so matching is automatic.
  • Microsoft Teams provides the email in most messages, and otherwise the platform resolves it from the sender's Entra ID identity.
  • WhatsApp, Telegram, and Discord do not expose an email. Those senders are either treated as anonymous, when the bot allows it, or asked to register.

When the sender matches an account, the conversation inherits that user's permissions, personal preferences, and memory — the same as if they had used web chat. Users can also route their own direct messages to a specific agent in My Profile > Channels & Bots.

docs.title: Good habits
docs.text:
• Connect one bot per platform and share it. Several agents can use the same bot with different scopes.
  • Set a receive whitelist before inviting the bot to busy channels, then widen it once the behavior is what you expect.
  • Turn on Only when mentioned for shared team channels, and leave it off for a dedicated support channel where the bot should answer everything.
  • Keep publish scopes tight. An agent that only needs to post a daily report needs one channel, not the whole workspace.
  • Review Routing on the bot card: it lists exactly which agents receive from and publish to that channel.
  • Rotate credentials on the messaging platform side, then paste the new value with Edit credentials. Fields left blank keep their stored value.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
The bot never answers. Check in this order: the bot card shows Connected; an agent has the channel enabled with Receive on; the channel is in the receive whitelist (or no whitelist is set); the bot has actually been invited to the channel. On group channels, also check whether Only when mentioned is on.

The bot answers in direct messages but not in channels. Almost always the receive whitelist, a missing invitation, or a missing mention.

The messaging platform rejects the webhook URL. Save the bot credentials in XTM One first. Verification requests are signature-checked, so the platform's URL test only succeeds once the secret is stored. Also confirm BASE_URL matches the public HTTPS address you pasted.

The bot answers twice. On Slack, this is caused by subscribing to both message.channels and app_mention. Keep one of the two.

An agent cannot post to a channel. The publish whitelist on the bot, the agent's own publish selection, or both. The effective scope is the overlap of the two.

Nothing works after changing the platform URL. The webhook URL is derived from BASE_URL. Update the endpoint on every messaging platform after the address changes.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Pick the platform you want to connect: Slack, Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, or Google Chat.

docs.title: Discord
docs.text:
Connecting Discord lets people talk to an agent in a server channel or a direct message, and lets agents post messages, reactions, and threads back.

Discord is the one channel that does not use a webhook: the platform opens a persistent connection to Discord itself. That changes one thing in the setup — the connection starts when the platform starts.

Read Channels and bots first for the concepts shared with the other platforms.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You need permission to create an application in the Discord developer portal, and to invite a bot to the target server.
  • You need administrator rights in XTM One.
  • You need to be able to restart the platform after saving the credentials.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Discord application
docs.text:
1. Go to discord.com/developers/applications and create a new application.
  2. Open Bot, click Reset Token, and copy the token.
  3. Under Privileged Gateway Intents, enable Message Content Intent. Without it, Discord delivers empty message content and the agent has nothing to answer.
  4. Optionally copy the application public key from General Information if you plan to use slash commands.

docs.title: Step 2: Invite the bot to your server
docs.text:
1. Open OAuth2 > URL Generator.
  2. Select the bot scope.
  3. Select the permissions Send Messages, Read Message History, and Add Reactions.
  4. Open the generated URL and invite the bot to the server.

docs.title: Step 3: Connect the bot in XTM One
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings > Channels & Bots and click Configure on the Discord card.
  2. Paste the bot token into Bot Token / Access Token.
  3. Optionally paste the application public key into Application public key. It is only needed for the interactions endpoint used by slash commands, and it enables signature verification on that endpoint.
  4. Click Save Channel.

Restart the platform after saving

The Discord connection is opened at platform startup. A bot saved on a running platform stays offline until the next restart.

docs.title: Step 4: Enable Discord on an agent
docs.text:
Open the agent, go to Configuration > Channels & Bots, and enable Discord:

  • Turn on Receive so the agent answers incoming messages.
  • Turn on Publish if the agent should post on its own.
  • Decide whether direct messages are allowed with Allow private, and whether people without an account may use the agent with Allow anonymous.

Whitelist entries are Discord channel IDs. To copy one, enable developer mode in Discord, then right-click a channel and choose Copy Channel ID.

docs.title: What to expect on Discord
docs.text:
• Discord does not expose an email address, so senders cannot be matched to an XTM One account automatically. Turn on Allow anonymous users if unknown senders should be served — the agent still receives the username as context.
  • Mentions are detected, so Only when mentioned works in server channels. Thread continuation does not: Discord has no thread identifier narrow enough to track, so a mention is needed for each new question when mention-only is on. /stop is unavailable for the same reason, while /reset works.
  • Answers longer than the Discord limit are split into several messages automatically.

docs.title: What the agent can do in Discord
docs.text: When Publish is on, the agent can send a message, read recent messages in a channel, list the channels it can see, create a thread, add a reaction, pin or unpin a message, and delete one of its own messages.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Restrict the receive whitelist to the channels where the bot is genuinely expected, since a server invitation exposes many channels at once.
  • Use Only when mentioned in community servers so the bot does not answer general chatter.
  • Use a dedicated agent with a narrow tool set when the server is public.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
The bot appears offline. The platform has not been restarted since the credentials were saved, or the token is wrong. Restart and check the platform logs for the Discord connection.

Messages arrive empty or are ignored. Message Content Intent is not enabled in the developer portal.

The bot answers in direct messages but not in channels. Check the channel permissions on the Discord side, the receive whitelist, and whether a mention is required.

Slash commands do nothing. The interactions endpoint URL must be configured in the developer portal, and the application public key must be stored in XTM One — Discord probes the endpoint with an invalid signature and expects it to be refused.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Connect another platform, such as Google Chat, or review how agents use channels in Agents.

docs.title: Google Chat
docs.text:
Connecting Google Chat lets people talk to an agent in a space or a direct message from Google Workspace, and lets agents post messages back into spaces.

Read Channels and bots first for the concepts shared with the other platforms.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You need a Google Cloud project and the rights to enable APIs and create service accounts in it.
  • You need a Google Workspace domain where the Chat app can be published to your users.
  • You need administrator rights in XTM One.
  • The platform must be reachable from the internet over HTTPS, because Google Chat posts messages to it.

docs.title: Step 1: Configure the Chat app in Google Cloud
docs.text:
1. In the Google Cloud Console, enable the Google Chat API for your project.
  2. Open the Chat API configuration page and set the app name, description, and avatar. This is what your users see in Google Chat.
  3. Enable the interactive features so the app can receive messages, and choose to receive them in spaces and direct messages.
  4. Under the connection settings, select HTTP endpoint URL and paste the webhook URL shown on the Google Chat card in XTM One — it ends with /api/channels/googlechat/webhook.
  5. Set the visibility so the people who should use the app can install it.

docs.title: Step 2: Create a service account
docs.text:
1. Go to IAM & Admin > Service Accounts and create a service account for the Chat app.
  2. Create a JSON key for it and download the file. This is how the platform sends messages back to Google Chat.
  3. Note the project number from the project overview page — it is the numeric identifier, not the project ID.

docs.title: Step 3: Connect the bot in XTM One
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings > Channels & Bots and click Configure on the Google Chat card.
  2. Paste the entire contents of the service account JSON key file into Bot Token / Access Token.
  3. Paste the project number into Google Cloud project number. This lets the platform verify that incoming requests really come from Google Chat.
  4. Click Save Channel.

Set the project number

Without it, the webhook accepts any request that reaches the URL. With it, every request must carry a valid Google-signed token issued for your project.

docs.title: Step 4: Enable Google Chat on an agent
docs.text:
Open the agent, go to Configuration > Channels & Bots, and enable Google Chat:

  • Turn on Receive so the agent answers incoming messages.
  • Turn on Publish if the agent should post on its own.
  • Adjust Allow anonymous, Allow private, and Only mention within what the bot allows.

Whitelist entries are space names, in the spaces/AAAAAAA form used by Google Chat.

docs.title: Step 5: Add the app to spaces
docs.text: In Google Chat, open the space and add the app from the space menu, or start a direct message with it. Like every other channel, the bot only sees the spaces it belongs to.

docs.title: What to expect on Google Chat
docs.text:
• Google Chat provides the sender's email address, so users are matched to their XTM One account automatically and get their own permissions, preferences, and memory.
  • Mentions are detected, so Only when mentioned works in spaces. Google Chat has real threads, so once the bot has answered in a thread it keeps following that thread without a new mention, and /stop mutes a specific thread.
  • There is no typing indicator in the Google Chat API, so a long answer arrives with no visible activity beforehand.
  • Files uploaded with a message reach the agent as files of the conversation, and a file sent without text is still answered. A file larger than the platform's 40 MB upload limit is not passed on, but the message is. A Google Drive file shared in a message is named to the agent with its link, but the Chat app cannot download it: Google Chat only serves uploaded content to an app, and Drive needs the user's own authorization, so an agent reads it through a Google integration.

docs.title: What the agent can do in Google Chat
docs.text: When Publish is on, the agent can send a message to a space, list the spaces it belongs to, read basic information about a space, and delete one of its own messages. It sends text only: Google Chat lets an app upload a file only on behalf of a signed-in user (media.upload requires user authentication), which the Chat app's service account is not.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Restrict app visibility in Google Workspace to the groups that should use it, then use the receive whitelist for finer control per space.
  • Use Only when mentioned in general-purpose spaces and leave it off in a space dedicated to the agent.
  • Keep the service account key in a secrets manager. Rotating it is a matter of creating a new key and pasting it with Edit credentials.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Google rejects the endpoint or the app never delivers messages. Confirm the Chat API is enabled, the app is configured for an HTTP endpoint, and the URL matches the one shown on the card.

Every request is rejected. The project number is wrong. It must be the numeric project number, not the project ID.

The app answers in direct messages but not in a space. It has not been added to that space, the space is not in the receive whitelist, or a mention is required.

The agent cannot post. The service account key is missing or invalid — the key is what authenticates outgoing messages, separately from the incoming webhook.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Connect another platform, such as Slack, or review how agents use channels in Agents.

docs.title: Microsoft Teams
docs.text:
Connecting Microsoft Teams lets your users chat with an agent from a team channel, a group chat, or a personal chat, and lets agents post messages, cards, and files back into Teams.

Teams has the longest setup of all channels because it involves three Microsoft surfaces: an Entra ID app registration for the identity and permissions, an Azure Bot resource for message delivery, and a Teams app package for installation in the tenant. Read Channels and bots first for the concepts shared with the other platforms.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You need an Entra ID (Azure AD) administrator, or someone who can grant admin consent for application permissions.
  • You need permission to upload a custom app to your Teams tenant, or a Teams administrator to do it for you.
  • You need administrator rights in XTM One.
  • The platform must be reachable from the internet over HTTPS, because Teams posts messages to it.

docs.title: Step 1: Register the application in Entra ID
docs.text:
1. In the Azure portal, go to Entra ID > App registrations > New registration.
  2. Note the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID from the overview page.
  3. Under Certificates & secrets, create a client secret and copy its value immediately — it is shown only once.
  4. Under API permissions, add the Microsoft Graph application permissions listed below, then click Grant admin consent. They must be application permissions, not delegated ones.

docs.title: Application permissions
docs.text: Permission Why it is needed Channel.ReadBasic.All List the channels the bot can work with Chat.Create Start a chat with a user Chat.Read.WhereInstalled Read messages in chats where the app is installed Chat.ReadWrite.WhereInstalled Read and write messages in those chats ChatMember.Read.WhereInstalled Read the members of those chats Team.ReadBasic.All List the teams the bot can work with

docs.title: Step 2: Create the Azure Bot resource
docs.text:
1. Create an Azure Bot resource in the Azure portal.
  2. Choose Single Tenant and Use existing app registration, using the application ID from step 1.
  3. In Settings > Configuration, set the messaging endpoint to the webhook URL shown on the Teams card in XTM One — it ends with /api/channels/teams/messages.
  4. In Channels, add the Microsoft Teams channel.

docs.title: Step 3: Connect the bot in XTM One
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings > Channels & Bots and click Configure on the Microsoft Teams card.
  2. Paste the application ID into App ID / Client ID.
  3. Paste the client secret into App Password / Client Secret.
  4. Paste the directory ID into Entra ID (Azure AD) Tenant ID.
  5. Click Save Channel. The card shows Connected and displays the webhook URL used in step 2.

The application ID is also what authenticates incoming traffic: XTM One validates the signed token on every Teams request against it, so requests that do not come from the Bot Framework are rejected.

docs.title: Step 4: Build and install the Teams app package
docs.text:
Teams needs an app package to install the bot in your tenant.

  1. Open the Teams Developer Portal and create the app.
  2. Use the manifest template offered by the Setup Guide button on the Teams card — it already carries your deployment name — and replace the placeholders with your application ID and domain.
  3. Declare the resource-specific consent permissions listed below under authorization.permissions.resourceSpecific.
  4. Package manifest.json, color.png, and outline.png into a .zip file.
  5. Install it through the Teams admin center, or sideload it if your tenant allows custom apps.

docs.title: Resource-specific permissions
docs.text:
Permission Why it is needed ChannelMessage.Read.Group Read channel messages in teams where the app is installed ChatMessage.Read.Chat Read messages in chats where the app is installed

Enable file support if users will send attachments

Set supportsFiles to true in the manifest for the bot to receive files sent in personal chats. Files shared in group chats and channels are retrieved through Graph and work regardless of this setting.

docs.title: Step 5: Enable Teams on an agent
docs.text:
Open the agent, go to Configuration > Channels & Bots, and enable Microsoft Teams:

  • Turn on Receive so the agent answers Teams messages, and optionally restrict it to specific channels.
  • Turn on Publish if the agent should post to Teams on its own, and pick the channels it may post to.
  • Adjust Allow anonymous, Allow private, and Only mention within what the bot allows.

The channel picker resolves team and channel identifiers for you. Group chats are never listed — their identifiers cannot be enumerated — so they are governed by Allow private, Only mention, and agent routing instead of by whitelists.

docs.title: Standard, private, and shared channels
docs.text:
Teams delivers messages differently depending on the channel type, and XTM One compensates for it.

  • In standard channels, every message is delivered to the bot, so mention behavior is entirely up to your settings.
  • In private and shared channels, Microsoft only delivers messages that @mention the bot. After the bot has answered a mention there, XTM One subscribes to that thread through Graph so follow-up messages keep reaching the agent without a new mention. Monitoring stops after seven days of inactivity, and the bot posts a short notice when it does.

docs.title: Graph notifications for private channels
docs.text:
Follow-ups in private and shared channels reach XTM One as Microsoft Graph notifications on <BASE_URL>/api/channels/teams/graph-notifications, a public endpoint Microsoft must be able to reach. Every subscription XTM One creates carries a random secret that Microsoft sends back with each notification; XTM One stores it encrypted and checks it, together with the subscription id, against what it recorded for the channel. Every notification of a delivery is checked before any work is queued for it, so one the verification policy below refuses costs nothing beyond that check. In the default mode, a forged notification that carries what earlier releases accepted (such as the copilot_ value for a channel with no record) is still acted on: one task per distinct message it names, the same message named twice in one delivery counting once. A delivery larger than 4 MiB, far above what Microsoft sends, is refused with HTTP 413, and one XTM One cannot check or record because its Redis does not answer gets HTTP 503, so Microsoft delivers it again later. A follow-up posted while no subscription could notify it - a subscription Microsoft removed, or one XTM One had to recreate - is read back from Microsoft Graph once the channel has a subscription again, up to four hours back, and answered once.

By default, XTM One also acts on a notification that earlier releases acted on without that proof: one carrying the secret of the subscriptions created before 2026-07-02 (copilot_ followed by the team id, which anyone who knows the team id can compute), or the channel's secret under another subscription id. Each case is logged as a warning, at most once every 15 minutes, and reported by the security audit in Settings > Security. Subscriptions created by an earlier release are kept and renewed as before, so nothing changes for your channels on upgrade.

To refuse every notification that does not prove its subscription, turn on Require verified integration notifications in Settings > Security > Security options, or set INTEGRATION_NOTIFICATIONS_REQUIRE_VERIFICATION=true - the switch that also refuses the unverified Slack, Microsoft Graph and LinkedIn notifications of integrations. The maintenance pass, which runs shortly after XTM One starts and then about once an hour, then replaces the subscriptions whose secret is derivable or can no longer be decrypted. Microsoft allows one subscription per channel, so it deletes the old one before creating the new one; what the old one was still delivering is accepted for four hours, and what was posted in between is read back from Microsoft Graph.

If Microsoft refuses the replacement

With the option on, a replacement deletes the old subscription first. If Microsoft Graph then refuses to create the new one, that channel's follow-ups stop until a later pass creates it, and the log says Graph subscription creation failed. With the option off, no subscription is deleted to be replaced.

docs.title: What the agent can do in Teams
docs.text:
When Publish is on, the agent gets Teams tools: send a message or an adaptive card to a channel, a personal chat, or a group chat, edit a message it already sent, read channel messages, chat messages, or thread replies, list teams and channels, list chats, upload a file to a channel, download a file it received, and delete one of its own channel messages.

Chat and group chat messaging is not governed by channel whitelists — those cover teams and channels. Long answers are split automatically, and images are delivered as separate cards because Teams rejects an activity carrying both text and attachments.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Grant admin consent once and keep the client secret in a password manager. When it expires, Teams stops delivering messages with no other symptom — use Edit credentials to paste the new value.
  • Note the secret expiry date in your calendar. Entra ID secrets are time-limited and this is the most common cause of a bot going silent months after a working setup.
  • Use Only when mentioned for busy team channels; thread continuation keeps follow-up questions working without a new mention.
  • Keep the publish whitelist to the channels the agent genuinely reports into.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
The bot is installed but never answers. Check the messaging endpoint in the Azure Bot resource, confirm the Teams channel is added there, and confirm an agent has Teams Receive enabled.

It worked and suddenly stopped. The client secret has almost certainly expired. Create a new one and update it in XTM One.

The bot answers in standard channels but not in a private one. That is expected until the bot has been @mentioned in the thread once. After that first mention, follow-ups are picked up for seven days.

Private-channel follow-ups after an upgrade or a SECRET_KEY change. By default nothing changes: a subscription created by an older release keeps working and is renewed, and after a SECRET_KEY change a notification naming the subscription recorded for its channel is still acted on, with a warning. With Require verified integration notifications on, such subscriptions are replaced by the maintenance pass instead (see Graph notifications for private channels). Nothing needs to change in Teams or Entra ID: the same permissions and the same public endpoint are used. Microsoft must be able to reach <BASE_URL>/api/channels/teams/graph-notifications, which also receives the subscription's lifecycle notifications.

Messages are rejected as unauthorized. The application ID stored in XTM One does not match the app the Azure Bot resource uses. They must be the same registration.

The bot cannot read files sent in a chat. Confirm supportsFiles is set in the manifest for personal chats, and that admin consent was granted for the Graph permissions used to fetch files shared in channels.

Mentions are not detected in group chats. Teams sometimes strips the mention data from the delivered message. XTM One re-reads the message through Graph to recover it, which requires the resource-specific permissions from step 4 to be declared and consented.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Connect another platform, such as Slack, or review how agents use channels in Agents.

docs.title: Slack
docs.text:
Connecting Slack lets your teams talk to an agent from a channel or a direct message, and lets agents post into Slack on their own — for example to publish a triage summary or reply in an incident thread.

Read Channels and bots first if you have not already: whitelists, mention behavior, and anonymous access work the same on every platform.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You need permission to create and install an app in your Slack workspace. In many workspaces this requires a Slack administrator to approve the installation.
  • You need administrator rights in XTM One.
  • The platform must be reachable from the internet over HTTPS, because Slack posts events to it.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Slack app
docs.text:
1. Go to api.slack.com/apps and select Create New App > From scratch. Give it a name and pick your workspace.
  2. Open OAuth & Permissions and add every scope from the table below under Bot Token Scopes.
  3. Open Agents & Assistants and turn on the App Agent toggle. This is what allows the typing indicator while an agent is thinking.
  4. Install the app to the workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token — it starts with xoxb-.
  5. Open Basic Information and copy the Signing Secret.

docs.title: Required scopes
docs.text:
Scope Why it is needed app_mentions:read Receive messages that @mention the bot assistant:write Show the typing indicator while the agent works channels:history Read messages in public channels the bot has joined channels:join Join public channels channels:read Read basic information about public channels chat:write Send messages as the bot groups:history Read messages in private channels the bot has joined groups:read Read basic information about those private channels im:history Read direct message history im:read Read basic direct message information im:write Start a direct message with someone users:read Read workspace profiles users:read.email Match Slack users to XTM One accounts by email

Adding scopes after installation requires reinstalling the app.

docs.title: Step 2: Connect the bot in XTM One
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings > Channels & Bots and click Configure on the Slack card.
  2. Paste the bot token into Bot Token / Access Token.
  3. Paste the signing secret into Slack signing secret for request verification.
  4. Click Save Channel. The card now shows Connected and displays the webhook URL to use in the next step.

Save the signing secret before configuring events

Slack signs its verification request, and XTM One refuses unsigned traffic. If the signing secret is not stored yet, Slack's URL check fails with a 401. Always complete this step before step 3.

docs.title: Step 3: Subscribe to events
docs.text:
1. Back in the Slack app, open Event Subscriptions and enable events.
  2. Set the Request URL to the webhook URL shown on the Slack card — it ends with /api/channels/slack/events. Slack verifies it immediately.
  3. Under Subscribe to bot events, add the events you need:
Event What it delivers message.im Direct messages with the bot — always add this one app_mention Messages that @mention the bot in a channel message.channels Every message in the public channels the bot has joined

The usual setup is message.im plus app_mention: the bot answers direct messages and mentions. For a dedicated support channel where the bot should answer everything, use message.im plus message.channels instead.

Never subscribe to both channel events

Subscribing to message.channels and app_mention together makes Slack fire two events for the same mention, and the bot answers twice.

docs.title: Step 4: Invite the bot to channels
docs.text: Type /invite @YourBotName in each channel where the bot should be active. The bot only sees channels it belongs to.

docs.title: Step 5: Enable Slack on an agent
docs.text:
Open the agent, go to Configuration > Channels & Bots, and enable Slack:

  • Turn on Receive so the agent answers incoming Slack messages, and optionally restrict it to specific channels.
  • Turn on Publish if the agent should post to Slack on its own, and pick the channels it may post to.
  • Adjust Allow anonymous, Allow private, and Only mention for this agent, within what the bot allows.

Channel whitelists on the bot use Slack channel IDs. The picker lists the channels the bot can see, so you rarely need to type an ID by hand.

docs.title: What the agent can do in Slack
docs.text:
When Publish is on, the agent gets Slack tools it can use during a conversation or an assignment: send a message, reply in a thread, read recent messages or a thread, list channels and users, look up a user, add or remove a reaction, pin or unpin a message, set a channel topic, and delete one of its own messages.

Replies are converted to Slack formatting automatically, so bold text and links render natively rather than as raw Markdown. Long answers are split into several messages instead of failing.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Use Only when mentioned in busy team channels. The bot still follows a thread it has already joined for about 24 hours, so people do not have to mention it in every reply.
  • Prefer a dedicated agent for public channels, with a narrow set of tools and knowledge bases.
  • Set the receive whitelist before inviting the bot to many channels, so a wide invitation does not become wide exposure.
  • Tell users about /reset to start a clean conversation and /stop to mute the bot in a thread that has moved on.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Slack rejects the request URL. The signing secret is missing or wrong in XTM One. Save it on the Slack card, then retry the URL verification.

The bot ignores channel messages. Check that it was invited to the channel, that the right event is subscribed, that the channel is in the receive whitelist, and that an agent has Slack Receive enabled.

Every mention gets two answers. Both message.channels and app_mention are subscribed. Remove one.

No typing indicator. The App Agent toggle is off or assistant:write is missing. Everything else keeps working.

The bot answers but cannot identify the user. The users:read and users:read.email scopes are required to match a Slack user to an account. Without them, senders are unknown and are only served if anonymous access is allowed.

A reply lands in the channel instead of the thread. Slack refuses thread replies on some message types; the platform falls back to posting in the channel rather than losing the answer.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Connect another platform, such as Microsoft Teams, or review how agents use channels in Agents.

docs.title: Telegram
docs.text:
Connecting Telegram lets people chat with an agent in a private conversation or a group, and lets agents post messages, photos, and polls back. It is the quickest channel to set up: a Telegram bot is created in a few messages with @BotFather.

Read Channels and bots first for the concepts shared with the other platforms.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You need a Telegram account.
  • You need administrator rights in XTM One.
  • The platform must be reachable from the internet over HTTPS, because Telegram posts messages to it.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the bot
docs.text:
1. Open Telegram and start a conversation with @BotFather.
  2. Send /newbot and follow the prompts to choose a name and a username.
  3. Copy the token that @BotFather returns. It looks like 123456:ABC-DEF....

docs.title: Step 2: Connect the bot in XTM One
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings > Channels & Bots and click Configure on the Telegram card.
  2. Paste the token into Bot Token / Access Token.
  3. Choose any string as a webhook secret and paste it into Webhook secret token (you define this; pass the same value as secret_token to setWebhook).
  4. Click Save Channel, and copy the webhook URL shown on the card.

docs.title: Step 3: Register the webhook with Telegram
docs.text:
Telegram has no console for this — you register the webhook with one API call, using the same secret you just saved:

curl -X POST "https://api.telegram.org/bot<YOUR_TOKEN>/setWebhook" -d "url=<YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL>" -d "secret_token=<YOUR_SECRET>"

Replace <YOUR_TOKEN> with the bot token, <YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL> with the URL from the Telegram card — it ends with /api/channels/telegram/webhook — and <YOUR_SECRET> with the webhook secret.

The secret is what authenticates Telegram

Telegram sends the secret back with every update, and XTM One checks it. If you skip it, any request that reaches the webhook URL is accepted. If it does not match what is stored, every update is rejected.

Send a message to the bot to confirm the connection works.

docs.title: Step 4: Enable Telegram on an agent
docs.text:
Open the agent, go to Configuration > Channels & Bots, and enable Telegram:

  • Turn on Receive so the agent answers incoming messages.
  • Turn on Publish if the agent should send messages on its own.
  • Decide whether private chats are allowed with Allow private, and whether people without an account may use the agent with Allow anonymous.

Whitelist entries are Telegram chat IDs.

docs.title: What to expect on Telegram
docs.text:
• Telegram does not expose an email address, so senders cannot be matched to an XTM One account automatically. Turn on Allow anonymous users if unknown senders should be served — the agent still receives the username and display name as context.
  • Mentions are detected, so Only when mentioned works in groups. Thread continuation does not: Telegram has no thread identifier narrow enough to track, so a mention is needed for each new question in a group where mention-only is on.
  • For the same reason, /stop is not available on Telegram. /reset works everywhere.
  • Photos, documents, audio, video, voice messages, and round video messages sent to the bot reach the agent, with their caption as the message. A file sent without a caption is still answered. Telegram lets a bot download files of up to 20 MB: a larger file is not passed on, but its caption is. Stickers are ignored.
  • By default, @BotFather hides group messages from bots. If the bot should read group conversations, send /setprivacy to @BotFather and disable privacy mode for it.

docs.title: What the agent can do in Telegram
docs.text:
When Publish is on, the agent can send a message, send a photo by URL, edit or delete one of its own messages, forward a message between chats, pin or unpin a message, create a poll, and read basic information about a chat, group, or channel.
