docs.text: free-text error string they carry today.

docs.title: Recharging a pool before its renewal date
docs.text:
An administrator can restore every pool on the platform without waiting for the anniversary, by redeeming a support code issued by Filigran in Settings → Quotas → Agent Failure Pool.

  • A code is a single signed token (XTMP-…) that the admin pastes in. It is verified offline, against the same Filigran trust anchor the platform already uses for license certificates — an air-gapped deployment can redeem one, and no secret is added to the platform.
  • Each code carries an expiry and an identifier, and is single-use: the identifier is recorded in support_code_redemptions on redemption, so a second attempt (or a code shared between two admins) is refused. Settings → Quotas lists the codes already redeemed, when, and by whom.
  • A code is normally bound to one PLATFORM_ID and refused elsewhere; Filigran can also issue a global code, redeemable on any platform.
  • Because verification is offline, a code cannot be revoked once issued — it can only expire. Ask support for a short validity when that matters.

Refusals are shown inline with the reason: not signed by Filigran, altered, expired on a date, issued for another platform, or already used on a date.

Why a pool instead of refunding every failure

Nothing available at the point of failure reliably separates "the provider was down" from "this prompt can never succeed". Crediting back every failure would make an endlessly retried, hopeless run free; crediting none spends a user's action quota on outages they did not cause. A small pool per agent covers the accidental case and charges the systematic one to the quota, with no classification to get wrong.

Sizing is environment-only

Both variables are environment-only, by design: what consumes the action quota belongs to whoever operates the deployment, not to whoever administers the tenant. Changing either one requires a restart. The admin screen is read-only apart from redeeming a support code.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Variable Required Default Description LOG_LEVEL No info debug, info, warning, error, critical. LOG_FORMAT No json json (structured) or console (human-readable). When unset, defaults to json in production or console when DEBUG=true.

docs.title: Email (SMTP)
docs.text:
Variable Required Default Description SMTP_HOSTNAME No — SMTP server hostname. SMTP_PORT No 587 SMTP port. SMTP_USERNAME No — SMTP authentication username. SMTP_PASSWORD No — SMTP authentication password. SMTP_FROM No — Sender address for outgoing emails. SMTP_STARTTLS No true Use STARTTLS. MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_ENABLED No false Email the platform's users when a boot (or switching AI on) finds the env-managed model catalog changed: DEFAULT_MODEL moved, or an LLM_PROVIDER_<P>_MODELS list gained or lost a model. One email per change names the new default model, the models now available and the ones retired ("New models available in your platform" when several arrive at once). Needs SMTP. Whether a change goes out is decided by the boot that records it, from its own configuration, so a pod still running the previous environment during a rolling deploy cannot drop it: a change recorded while this is off (or without SMTP) is sent by a later boot that has both, within 7 days, as long as nobody was emailed about it and it still describes the live catalog. What became of each change (queued, skipped and why, sent to how many) is logged at WARNING. A change waits until the env catalog has stayed unchanged for MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_SETTLE_MINUTES, so the changes of successive deploys reach the users as one email. Emails go out in English from the scheduler, a batch per minute, oldest change first, never twice to the same person: an email whose delivery could not be confirmed (the connection dropped mid-send, a worker stopped) is not retried. Announcements an administrator sends from Settings > AI Models do not depend on this switch (see Emailing users about model changes). MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_RECIPIENTS No all all (every active user) or admins, for the changes a boot finds. Announcements sent from Settings go to every active user. The bootstrap ADMIN_EMAIL account is never emailed. MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_BATCH_SIZE No 20 Emails sent per scheduler tick (one a minute); the rest follows on the next ticks. Keep it under your mail server's sending limit: a hosted mailbox allowing 200 emails an hour needs 3 or less. MODEL_CATALOG_EMAILS_SETTLE_MINUTES No 30 How long, in minutes (0 to 1440), the env-managed model catalog must stay unchanged before the change a boot found is emailed. Every env change deployed before then (a corrected rollout, a second release, a rolling restart with new values) is added to the same email and restarts the wait, and a change reverted meanwhile is never sent. 0 sends from the next scheduler tick. Announcements sent from Settings are never held. MODEL_CATALOG_CHANGES_WINDOW_HOURS No 24 How far back, in hours (1 to 168), the model list saves an administrator has not emailed yet are combined into the model changes Settings > AI Models offers to email. Every save is kept; a model added then retired within the window (or the reverse) cancels out, and a change the live catalog no longer holds is left out.

Every email the platform sends (password reset, invitation, model announcements) follows the Filigran email layout and loads its images from <FRONTEND_URL>/email-assets/: the recipients' mail client must reach FRONTEND_URL to show the logos.

docs.title: Security feature flags
docs.text:
Variable Required Default Description AGENT_TOOLS_STRICT_ADMIN_ACCESS No false Keep every agent tool of an admin - the agent builder, the agent trace inspection and the work-items delegation, in chat and on the XTM One MCP server - to the admin's own, group-shared and company-managed objects, like every other caller: the agents, assignments, runs, traces, evaluations, knowledge bases, skills and other entities a tool looks up, lists or binds. The admin role still counts where a tool checks a permission (a company-managed object, an admin-only setting). By default an admin's agent reaches everything, as the admin does in the UI and through the REST API; the Security Audit reports the default while an agent carries one of these tools, chat is on (the General Assistant offers the agent builder in every conversation) or the XTM One MCP server is enabled. Also in Settings > Security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. DISABLE_CODE_INTERPRETER No true (xtm_one mode) Disable code interpreter at infra level. Also in Settings > Security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. DISABLE_CUSTOM_TOOLS No true (xtm_one mode) Disable custom tools at infra level. Also in Settings > Security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. CUSTOM_TOOL_SANDBOX No auto Custom tool execution mode: auto, docker, subprocess, opensandbox. opensandbox delegates to an OpenSandbox-managed container (also used by the code interpreter) and requires the OpenSandbox connection variables below. DISABLE_SANDBOX_QUOTA_USAGE No false Opt out of per-user sandbox usage counting (quota_usage rows with usage_type="sandbox", alongside the existing LLM-proxy/agentic usage). Counted by default; set true for self-hosted/on-prem deployments that manage their own sandbox infrastructure independently of hosted usage-based billing. Restart required to take effect. INTEGRATION_NOTIFICATIONS_REQUIRE_VERIFICATION No false Refuse every Slack event on /api/v1/integrations/notifications/slack and every Microsoft Graph change notification the platform cannot authenticate, those of the Teams bot's private and shared channels on /api/channels/teams/graph-notifications included. By default a Slack integration with no usable signing secret keeps receiving its events without a verified signature, and a Graph subscription recorded without a clientState keeps working, each with a warning in the log and a Security Audit finding. A delivery that a stored Slack signing secret or a Graph clientState does not prove never reaches what that secret or clientState protects, whatever the setting. The same setting limits what the admin OAuth app's webhook (/api/hooks/providers/<provider>) and the LinkedIn notification URL deliver to the admin app's integrations the agent owner may use (for a GitHub App event, those recording its installation or, recording none, whose own token sees it), and drops a LinkedIn notification when no LinkedIn client secret is configured; by default they reach what they reached before, with a warning and a Security Audit finding. That webhook accepts, without a check, a delivery for a provider whose OAuth default holds no webhook secret, and by default one for a provider with no OAuth default (with the setting on, such a provider reaches nothing); both are reported the same way. For the Teams bot's private and shared channels, a notification that does not carry the subscription id and the random secret (clientState) XTM One recorded for its channel is still acted on by default whenever earlier releases acted on it, with a warning and a Security Audit finding, and the subscriptions created before 2026-07-02 (whose secret anyone who knows the team id can compute) are kept and renewed; with the setting on, such a notification is refused, the maintenance pass replaces those subscriptions and the ones whose secret can no longer be decrypted (if Microsoft Graph refuses to create a replacement, that channel's follow-ups stop until a later pass creates it), and what a refused notification held back is read back from Microsoft Graph, up to four hours back. Nothing to set on upgrade. See Real-time Slack, Microsoft Graph or LinkedIn events do not arrive and Microsoft Teams. Also in Settings > Security (Require verified integration notifications); the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. PROMPT_GUARD_SCANNED_TOOLS No empty The tools whose results the connected prompt guard screens, comma-separated: a tool's registered name for a built-in, integration or MCP tool (for example web_fetch,search_jira_issues), and custom:<id> for a custom tool, with the custom tool's id - it stays screened when its owner renames it. While a company-managed Nova integration is connected, the guard evaluates what a listed tool returns to an agent - the text the agent reads, followed by the text of the files the result attaches (images excluded) - and records each rule match in the audit log (Security alert, surface tool_result, with the tool, the rules and their action). The result itself is left exactly as it is, and the evaluation runs beside the agent, which does not wait for it. Empty by default: no tool result is screened, and an agent run does what it did before the setting existed. Also in Settings > Security (Tools screened by the prompt guard), where the tools are picked from a list; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_TOOL_RESULTS No false With PROMPT_GUARD_SCANNED_TOOLS set, withhold a screened tool result that a block rule matches: the agent reads a short refusal naming the tool instead, without the files the result carried, and the result is not reused for an identical call. The agent then waits for the guard's verdict on each screened result before it continues (at most 20 seconds each, the results of one parallel batch evaluated together, four at a time in each platform or worker process); a guard that fails or runs out of time lets the result through. Off, a match is recorded and the result reaches the agent as it is; the security audit reports that log-only mode while a guard is connected. Also in Settings > Security (Withhold tool results a guard rule blocks); the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. PUBLIC_WIDGET_STRICT_RENDERING No false Public chat widget: show only the images the platform serves in an answer (any other image becomes a link the visitor can open, so the visitor's browser never fetches a URL an answer chose), open every link of an answer in a new tab, and render answers without inline styles, presentational markup (align, bgcolor, <font>, ...), SVG or MathML, with links of the http, https, mailto and tel schemes only. By default answers render as they always did: an image from any http(s) host is shown, an HTML link without a target opens in the page, and inline styles, presentational markup, SVG / MathML drawings and links of any other scheme (msteams:, sms:, ...) are kept. Script is removed in both modes: script elements, event handlers, javascript: / vbscript: / data: URLs, frames, forms and embedded objects. Links that launch a Windows program with a public exploitation history (ms-msdt:, search-ms:, ms-officecmd:, ms-appinstaller:, ...) are removed in both modes too, their text kept, as they are in the Office add-in; app links (slack:, msteams:, ...) and the Office document links (ms-word:, ms-excel:, ...) keep working. The security audit (Settings → Security) reports the default while a widget is enabled. Also in Settings > Security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. PUBLIC_WIDGET_UPLOAD_RETENTION_DAYS No 7 Public chat widget visitor uploads (see Visitor uploads on the public chat widget): the files a visitor attached are deleted once their conversation has had no message for this many days; a file uploaded and never sent with a message is deleted after a day, and the files of a deleted conversation within the hour. A value below 1 is read as 1: the retention cannot be switched off. SVG_STRICT_RENDERING No false SVGs a model is shown (a chat upload, a user-message image, a tool result such as an agent reading back the diagram it drew): refuse, instead of rendering, an SVG that declares an XML entity or references anything outside itself - a file path, an http(s) URL or another document, in an <image>, <feImage> or <use> or a url(...) in an attribute. By default such an SVG renders with that reference dropped - what resvg drew there on its own, as it follows only references inside the document - and an internal entity (an Adobe Illustrator export declares its namespaces this way) is expanded within a bound. Nothing is fetched or read from disk in either mode, and a nested SVG embedded as a data: URI (draw.io icons) is checked under the same rules. The security audit (Settings → Security) reports the default. PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_GENERAL_ASSISTANT No false While a prompt guard (the Nova integration) is connected, a General Assistant message is evaluated before the model is called and every rule match is written to the audit log (security_alert, source: nova_guard, surface: chat_message, chat_surface: general_assistant). By default the message is answered even when a block rule matched (the entry records rule_action: block, action: allowed): the General Assistant was not guarded before, so nothing it answers today is refused on upgrade. Set true to refuse such a message with the guard's message, as agent chat always does. The security audit reports which of the two applies while a guard is connected. Also in Settings > Security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field. PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_PUBLIC_WIDGET No false The same for a public chat widget visitor's message (chat_surface: public_widget). A visitor has no account, so the entry is written as the guard (system:nova_guard) and attached to the admin account the widget acts as (ADMIN_EMAIL). With true, a refused message reaches no model and its agentic action is given back. PROMPT_GUARD_MODEL_OUTPUT No off Evaluate the model's answer with the connected prompt guard (the Nova integration): off, log or block. Covered: the final answer of every top-level agent turn (web chat, the REST chat API, channel bots, the chat embedded in OpenCTI / OpenAEV, A2A, the MCP agent endpoints, the LLM proxy, the browser extension, background tasks, flows), the General Assistant's (a transfer's included) and the public widget's. Not covered: a consult's or a transfer's inner answer (its parent's answer is), evaluation runs, the OpenAEV autonomous run's cycles after the first, and assignment runs, whose result reaches their owner and which act on the outside world through write tools. off evaluates nothing. log returns every answer unchanged and at once, and evaluates it in the background (at most 4 at a time per process and 64 pending, 20 seconds each, the first 20,000 characters); a match is written to the audit log (security_alert, surface: model_output, action: allowed). block evaluates an answer before it is delivered and replaces one a block rule matches with a withheld notice (action: block), where the answer is delivered whole: the REST chat API, channel bots, A2A, the MCP endpoints, the LLM proxy, the browser extension, background tasks, the widget's non-streaming endpoint and a transfer from the General Assistant. A streamed answer (web chat, the streaming chat embedded in OpenCTI / OpenAEV, the widget's stream) has already been shown when it is complete, so in block it is evaluated and audited after delivery as in log, with streamed: true, and never withheld. An evaluation that fails or runs out of time delivers the answer. With no guard connected nothing is evaluated whatever the value. Write-tool arguments (an email body, a ticket comment) are not evaluated. The security audit reports the value while a guard is connected. Also in Settings > Security; the variable, when set, wins and locks the field.

Embedding the chat widget on a site with its own Content-Security-Policy

The widget (/api/v1/public/widget.js) runs inside the page of the site that embeds it, in a Shadow DOM, so that site's Content-Security-Policy applies to everything it loads. If the site sends one, it must allow:

  • script-src: the XTM One origin (the widget script);
  • connect-src: the XTM One origin (the API calls and the streamed answers);
  • img-src: the XTM One origin (the widget logo and the images the platform serves), plus the hosts answers link images from - by default an answer can show an image from any http(s) host, and with PUBLIC_WIDGET_STRICT_RENDERING=true it shows only the platform's own;
  • style-src: 'unsafe-inline' and https://fonts.googleapis.com;
  • font-src: https://fonts.gstatic.com.

'unsafe-inline' in style-src is the only choice today: the widget styles itself with a <style> element it builds at run time and with an inline style attribute in its markup, and it supports no nonce. A hash cannot replace it either: the stylesheet changes with every widget release, and a hash does not cover a style attribute without 'unsafe-hashes'. Without it the widget's styles are blocked and it renders unstyled.

In both rendering modes, an image the platform stores for the visitor's session - a file or a generated image an answer shows by its platform address (/api/v1/chat/files/<id>, /api/v1/chat/images/<id>) - is shown inline and loads from the XTM One origin through the visitor's own session (/api/v1/public/chat/<token>/sessions/<session>/...): the visitor needs no platform account, and the platform refuses any file or image the session does not own.

docs.title: Visitor uploads on the public chat widget
docs.text:
A widget visitor has no account. Each agent's widget can let its visitors attach files to their messages: Allow visitor uploads in the agent's Configuration > Channels > Web Exposure, off for every widget until its owner turns it on. The security audit reports the widgets that allow it (control web.public_widget_uploads, a warning while one does). With it on, the widget shows an attach button and takes a pasted screenshot or a dropped file. The agent receives each file as in the web chat - a document as its text (the first 50,000 characters, what the chat upload message carries), an image by its pixels, and every file's id for the tools that take a file - but a document never reaches the model as its native bytes, even with a provider that reads PDF or Office files natively: the model reads exactly the text the prompt guard evaluated. What bounds an anonymous uploader:

  • Types: PDF, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx, .xls), PowerPoint (.pptx), text and data files (.txt, .md, .csv, .tsv, .json, .jsonl, .ndjson, .xml, .yaml, .yml, .log, .html, .htm) and raster images (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp), decided on the file name and checked against the file's content: an image is decoded as the format its name says and may declare at most 20,000 pixels a side and 50 million in all, an Office document must be an Office package whose parts and expanded size are bounded (no archive under another name). The type the browser declares is ignored. No SVG, archive, audio or video.
  • Size and load: the chat upload limit, 40 MB a file. A larger body is refused on its declared length before it is read, and cut off past the limit when it declares none. Each platform process reads at most 4 visitor files at once, uploads and the documents of messages being sent alike; past that a visitor is told to retry (503 with Retry-After), and a message refused this way keeps its files in the widget. Every image and Office file is decoded, and every document read, when it is uploaded, in a worker process of its own, never on the threads the platform's own document work uses: a file that takes more than 30 seconds, or more than 2 GB of address space where the operating system lets that cap be set (Linux), is stopped and refused (422). A visitor who disconnects mid-upload still counts against those 4 files until the store ends, and leaves no stored file that the quotas and the retention do not count - unless the object store and the database both fail at that moment, in which case the object's key is written to the error log for an operator to remove.
  • Budgets: 20 uploads an hour per client address and 200 an hour per widget across all its visitors. Both refuse while Redis cannot be reached, whatever RATE_LIMIT_FAIL_MODE says.
  • Storage: 10 files and 100 MB per conversation, 2 GB per widget across its conversations, checked before the body is read and again when the file is written.
  • Content: while a prompt guard (the Nova integration) is connected, the text the model will read of each document is evaluated before the file is stored, and a match is written to the audit log (security_alert, surface: widget_upload, as the guard, attached to the admin account the widget acts as). With PROMPT_GUARD_BLOCK_PUBLIC_WIDGET=true, a file a block rule matches is refused.
  • Reach: a visitor's file belongs to its conversation and to no user. Only the visitor's own session downloads it (an image inline, every other file as a download, never kept by a cache); on the platform only administrators can open it.
  • Retention: deleted once the conversation has had no message for PUBLIC_WIDGET_UPLOAD_RETENTION_DAYS (7 by default), a file never sent with a message after a day, and the files of a deleted conversation within the hour - the stored object first, then its record, so an object store that does not answer leaves both for the next hourly pass. Turning the switch off stops new uploads; the files already attached follow the same retention.

Every refused upload says why - its type, its size, a budget, the conversation's or the widget's storage, the content check - and the widget shows the reason next to the file.

docs.title: Settings > Security options
docs.text:
These security options are set in Settings > Security by an administrator, or by their environment variable. The rule is the one the AI Models defaults and the Langfuse card follow: the variable, when set (and not blank), wins - the field is then shown read-only with the variable's name ("Set by environment variable X") and a change to it is refused. With the variable unset, the value saved in Settings > Security applies; with nothing saved, the default below applies, which is the platform's behaviour before the options reached the UI. A change made on one replica applies on every web and worker process within 5 seconds.

One option is fixed in xtm_one mode (and ai_disabled): quotas are part of the XTM One licence, so Quotas when their store is unreachable is always closed - while the quota store cannot be reached, agentic work is refused rather than run unmetered, requests with no account behind them included (anonymous channel users, the public chat widget, the platform MCP key). A due automation (a scheduled, webhook or integration-event assignment run, a background task) is not refused but held: it is shown as Held, is charged once it runs, and runs by itself once the store answers again, bounded by AI_UNAVAILABLE_HOLD_MAX_SECONDS. A store that refuses the platform's credentials (a wrong password, an ACL denial) is a configuration error, not an outage: that work is refused at once. The field is shown read-only with that reason and a change to it is refused; QUOTA_FAIL_MODE has no effect (set to open, it is ignored with a warning at startup), and a value already saved in Settings > Security is kept but not applied. In copilot / dev mode the option follows the rule above.

Settings > Security field Variable Default Trust proxy headers TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS false (prefer FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS) Canonical client addresses CLIENT_IP_STRICT false Require HTTPS for runner enrollment and MCP tokens CREDENTIAL_TRANSPORT_STRICT false IPv6 rate-limit prefix length RATE_LIMIT_IPV6_PREFIX 128 (32-128) Rate limits when Redis is unreachable RATE_LIMIT_FAIL_MODE open Quotas when their store is unreachable QUOTA_FAIL_MODE always closed in xtm_one mode (not configurable, the variable is ignored), open in copilot / dev Minimum password length MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH 8 (1-1024) Password reset link lifetime (hours) PASSWORD_RESET_EXPIRE_HOURS 24 (1-720) Invitation link lifetime (hours) INVITATION_EXPIRE_HOURS 168 (1-720) MCP client self-registration MCP_DCR_ENABLED true A2A_ALLOW_INSECURE_LOOPBACK false Require webhook secrets WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_SECRET false Exact event matching for every trigger WEBHOOK_EXACT_EVENT_MATCHING false Require verified integration
